BURHAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p284/r2.claim: Yā Sīn preposes “from the city's farthest end” to make readers wonder whether the whole city rejected the messengers or whether one person differed; al-Qaṣaṣ keeps the ordinary order.
BURHAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: قدم المجرور على المرفوع لاشتمال ما قبله من سوء معاملة أصحاب القرية الرسل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r4.claim: Once the killing secret spread, Pharaoh’s people naturally planned to eliminate Moses; the city center of the rulers lay far from the Israelite settlement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r4.anchor: would have fumed with anger against him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r5.claim: The man warning Moses was probably the believing member of Pharaoh’s clan later described in Sūrah al-Mu’min; his rush to Moses shows genuine concern.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r5.anchor: in all probability, it seems that this was the same person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p532/r6.claim: The well-wisher introduced himself and advised Moses to leave immediately.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r4.claim: The courtier’s run to Moses’ settlement, despite being among Pharaoh’s courtiers, exemplified his sympathy and concern.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r4.anchor: example of this sympathy and concern

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r3.claim: The man arriving from the far end of the city may be the believer from Pharaoh's family; al-Kalbi names him Jibril ibn Shamaun, al-Dahhak calls him Shamaun ibn Ishaq, and another view says he was someone else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r3.anchor: قيل: هو مؤمن آل فرعون، وكان ابن عم فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r4.claim: Yasʿa means he hastened; من أقصى المدينة and يسعى can both describe the man, though the latter can be circumstantial or the former attached to جاء. The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's restriction because Sibawayh allows a bare indefinite noun to take a circumstantial clause.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r5.claim: The ملأ are Pharaoh's state notables; يأتمرون means they consult, supported by al-Namr ibn Tawlab's poetry, while Ibn Qutayba glosses it as ordering one another, citing 2:233.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r5.anchor: إن الملأ، وهم وجوه أهل دولة فرعون، يأتمرون: يتشاورون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r6.claim: The phrase لك متعلق either to an omitted statement that the man is Moses' adviser, as an explanation, or to الناصحين despite that word's adjectival construction; grammarians report three positions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r6.anchor: ولك: متعلق إما بمحذوف، أي ناصح لك من الناصحين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r7.claim: Moses trusted the man's warning, escaped his pursuers, and took an unfamiliar route alone while trusting and asking God to save him from the wrongdoers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p294/r7.anchor: وكان موسى لا يعرف ذلك الطريق، ولم يصحب أحدا، فسلك مجهلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

JISHUMI:v8p5478/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r10.claim: Iʾtimār means consultation and people consulting each other, as in the cited poetic line.
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r10.anchor: والائتمار: المشاورة وأمر بعضهم لبعض، ائتمر القوم وتآمروا

JISHUMI:v8p5478/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r11.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r11.claim: A poet says that people have adopted a new custom and deliberate together over every event; the line illustrates consultation.
JISHUMI:v8p5478/r11.anchor: أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة ... وفي كل حادثة يؤتمر

TABRISI:28:17-20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:17-20/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:17-20/r7.claim: In “I am a well-wisher to you,” the lām cannot attach to the relative clause's adjective because that clause cannot govern before its relative; it attaches to an understood word instead.
TABRISI:28:17-20/r7.anchor: لا يجوز أن تتعلق اللام في لك بالناصحين لأن الصلة لا تعمل فيما قبل الموصول

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says yasʿā may be a modifier of “a man” or a circumstantial accusative, since “from the farthest part of the city” has already specified him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) يسعى يجوز ارتفاعه وصفا لرجل

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r2.claim: Iʾtimār means consultation: two people each advise the other or point him toward an action; here the chiefs are consulting about Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r2.anchor: والائتمار التشاور يقال الرجلان ( يتآمران ) يأتمران

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r3.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r3.claim: Most exegetes identify the man as the believer from Pharaoh’s family, who hurries out of concern to warn Moses that the chiefs are consulting to kill him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r3.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن هذا الرجل مؤمن آل فرعون

BURSEVI:v6p285/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r11.claim: The warning man is Khirbil, a believer from Pharaoh’s household and his cousin.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r11.anchor: فخرج مؤمن من آل فرعون وهو ابن عمه ليخبر موسى كما قال {وجاء رجل} وهو خربيل

BURSEVI:v6p285/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285/r12.claim: Aqṣā al-madīna may mean the far end of the city, or that the man came from that far end; the root denotes distance.
BURSEVI:v6p285/r12.anchor: يقال : قصوت عنه وأقصيت أبعدت والقصي البعيد.

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r1.claim: The participle describes the man hurrying in his walk until he reached Moses.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r1.anchor: {يسعى} صفة رجل أي يسرع في مشيه حتى وصل إلى موسى

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r2.claim: Al-malaʾ refers to Pharaoh’s leading nobles.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r2.anchor: {قال يا موسى إن الملا} أشراف قوم فرعون

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r3.claim: Yaʾtamirūna means consulting about Moses; it is called iʾtimār because each person commands the others and accepts their commands.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r3.anchor: يتشاورون بسببك وإنما سمي التشاور ائتمارا

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r4.claim: The man warns that the nobles intend to kill Moses and tells him to leave the city.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r4.anchor: {ليقتلوك فاخرج} من المدينة {إنى لك من الناصحين} في أمري إياك بالخروج

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r5.claim: The speaker says he is advising Moses well by telling him to get out.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r5.anchor: {إنى لك من الناصحين} في أمري إياك بالخروج.

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r6.claim: The lām clarifies to whom advice is addressed; it is not governed by nāṣiḥīn, since a relative’s complement cannot precede it.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r6.anchor: لأن معمول الصلة لا يتقدم الموصول وهو اللام في الناصح.

RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.claim: Al-Razi reproaches the servant for siding with Satan: Satan once worshipped God but was expelled for refusing to honor Adam, then opposed humankind while people keep loving and obeying him; the response is to declare enmity through seeking refuge in God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.anchor: يا عبدي ما أنصفتني أتدري لأي شيء تكدر ما بيني وبين الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.claim: Satan swore to Adam that he was a sincere adviser yet caused his expulsion from Paradise; since Satan now swears to mislead people, his treatment of them can only be worse.
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.anchor: أما إن نظرت إلى قصة أبيك فإنه أقسم بأنه له من الناصحين ثم كان عاقبة ذلك الأمر أنه سعى في إخراجه من الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.claim: Seeking refuge specifically in the name Allah invokes the one worthy of worship, whose power, knowledge and wisdom make Him a complete deterrent from wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.anchor: لأن هذا الاسم أبلغ في كونه زاجرا عن المعاصي من سائر الأسماء والصفات لأن الإله هو المستحق للعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.claim: Power alone does not deter: a thief may know a ruler is powerful yet steal because he thinks the ruler is unaware.
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r4.anchor: لأن السارق يعلم قدرة السلطان وقد يسرق ماله لأن السارق عالم بأن ذلك السلطان وإن كان قادرا إلا أنه غير عالم

RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.claim: Power and knowledge alone still do not deter if a ruler tolerates wrongdoing; complete deterrence requires wisdom that rejects vile acts, which refuge in Allah entails.
RAZI-FULL:v1p83#2/r5.anchor: فالقدرة والعلم لا يكفيان في حصول الزجر لأن الملك إذا رأى منكرا إلا أنه لا ينهي عن المنكر

STUDYQURAN:28:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r1.claim: Some identify the man who warned Moses as a believer from Pharaoh’s people.
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r1.anchor: Some commentators say that the man who came running was

STUDYQURAN:28:20/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r2.claim: Others identify the man as an Israelite.
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r2.anchor: people of Pharaoh” (Q, R) or an Israelite (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:28:20/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r3.claim: Some think the Israelite’s loud words to Moses in verse 19 exposed his deed to others.
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r3.anchor: what the Israelite said to him in v. 19 was loud enough to be heard by others

STUDYQURAN:28:20/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r4.claim: Malāʾ, translated notables, can also mean a council or group of leaders.
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r4.anchor: can also mean “council” or “group of leaders.”

STUDYQURAN:28:20/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r5.claim: The Quran portrays notables as often hostile to prophets, including those of Sheba, Quraysh, Hūd, Shuʿayb, and Joseph’s king.
STUDYQURAN:28:20/r5.anchor: The Quran also discusses the notables—a class of people who were often the most hostile to the prophets—of the Queen of Sheba

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r1.claim: After someone heard and spread the Israelite’s remark to the slain man’s people, Pharaoh sought Moses and ordered his death; a man then warned Moses and urged him to leave Egypt.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r1.anchor: فأرسل فرعون الذباحين لقتل موسى، فأخذوا الطريق الأعظم

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r2.claim: The Egyptian told his people what he had heard; Pharaoh sent executioners along the main road, while a partisan of Moses took a shortcut and reached Moses first with the warning.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " انطلق الفرعوني الذي كان يقاتل الإسرائيلي إلى قومه، فأخبرهم بما سمع

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Egyptian informed the council, which plotted to kill Moses; people also identified the arriving man as the believer from Pharaoh’s household.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " أعلمهم القبطي الذي هو عدو لهما، فأتمر الملأ ليقتلوه

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says people used to report that the arriving man was the believer from Pharaoh’s household.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r4.anchor: قال: كنا نحدث أنه مؤمن آل فرعون

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh ordered Moses seized and searched for along side paths, assuming the young Moses could not find the way; Moses took those paths as the messenger came to warn him.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " ذهب القبطي، يعني الذي كان يقاتل الإسرائيلي، فأفشى عليه أن موسى هو الذي قتل الرجل

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r6.claim: Abū Bakr b. ʿAbd Allāh’s companions say the Egyptian told the slain man’s family that Moses had killed him; Moses fled when he learned they knew, and escaped his pursuers.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن أصحابه، قالوا: " لما سمع القبطي قول الإسرائيلي لموسى

TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r7.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Najīḥ says the Egyptian was the one who spread the report against Moses.
TAB-FULL:v18p198#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح: سعى القبطي

TAB-FULL:v18p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says an enemy heard them and spread what he heard.
TAB-FULL:v18p199/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: «سمع ذلك عدو، فأفشى عليهما»

TAB-FULL:v18p200/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r1.claim: The man is identified as a believer from Pharaoh’s household; his name is reported as Samʿān, while another view gives Shimʿān.
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، أخبرني وهب بن سليمان، عن شعيب الجبئي، قال: " اسمه شمعون

TAB-FULL:v18p200/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj, citing Wahb b. Sulaymān from Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾī, names the man Shimʿān.
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، أخبرني وهب بن سليمان، عن شعيب الجبئي، قال: " اسمه شمعون

TAB-FULL:v18p200/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq names him Samʿān and reports that he came as Pharaoh’s council had agreed to kill Moses and advised him to flee.
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " أصبح الملأ من قوم فرعون قد أجمعوا لقتل موسى

TAB-FULL:v18p200/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r4.claim: Qatāda reports the man’s arrival at Moses’ far-off location and his warning that the council meant to kill him.
TAB-FULL:v18p200/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} [القصص: 20] إلى موسى {قال يا موسى إن الملأ

TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r1.claim: The city’s farthest edge means the outskirts of Pharaoh’s city.
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} [القصص: 20] قال: يعجل

TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says “yasʿā” means that the man hurried; it does not necessarily mean he ran.
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} [القصص: 20] قال: يعجل، ليس بالشد

TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r3.claim: The council’s leaders are consulting, deliberating, and considering what to do about Moses.
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r3.anchor: أشراف قوم فرعون ورؤساءهم يتآمرون بقتلك، ويتشاورون ويرتئون فيك

TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r4.claim: An anonymous poem uses “taʾtamir” to mean considering or intending something.
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r4.anchor: ما تأتمر فينا فأمرك … في يمينك أو شمالك

TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r5.speaker: النمر بن تولب
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r5.claim: Al-Namir b. Tawlab’s verse uses “yuʾtamar” for mutual consultation and deliberation.
TAB-FULL:v18p200#2/r5.anchor: ومنه قول النمر بن تولب: [البحر المتقارب] أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة … وفي كل حادثة يؤتمر

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r4.claim: Iʾtimār means consultation, and naṣīḥa (sincere advice) is the opposite of treachery.

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r5.claim: The phrase “from the farthest part of the city” grammatically qualifies “came”; the story suggests the conspiracy was at Pharaoh’s order and the man came from there to warn Moses.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r5.anchor: والظاهر كون قوله { من أقصى المدينة } قيدا لقوله { جاء } فسياق القصة يعطي أن الإئتمار كان عند فرعون

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r6.claim: The inference that the palace Pharaoh lived in stood beyond the city is reinforced by the story’s wording about the man coming from its far end.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r6.anchor: وهذا الاستئناس من الكلام يؤيد ما تقدم أن قصر فرعون الذي كان يسكنه كان خارج المدينة

TABRISI:28:18-20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r9.claim: The man came from the city’s far edge, took a nearby shortcut to reach Moses first, and hurried to warn him.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r9.anchor: أي آخرها فاختصر طريقا قريبا حتى سبقهم إلى موسى

TABRISI:28:18-20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r10.claim: The man is identified as Ḥizqīl, the believer in Pharaoh’s household; other reports name him Shimʿūn or Samʿān.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r10.anchor: وكان الرجل حزقيل مؤمن آل فرعون. وقيل: رجل اسمه شمعون

TABRISI:28:18-20/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:28:18-20/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains yaʾtamirūna as the nobles consulting together about Moses.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r11.anchor: أي يتشاورون فيك عن أبي عبيدة

TABRISI:28:18-20/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r12.claim: Another explanation is that some of the nobles were ordering others.
TABRISI:28:18-20/r12.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة. وقيل: يأمر بعضهم

TABRISI:28:18-20/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:18-20/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:18-20/r13.claim: The warning is to leave Egypt; Arabic permits both naṣaḥtuhu and naṣaḥtu lahu for ‘I advised him.’
TABRISI:28:18-20/r13.anchor: في هذا يقال نصحته ونصحت له

THALABI:v7p242/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p242/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when Pharaoh sent executioners, a supporter of Moses took a shortcut from the city's far end, reached him before them, and warned him.
THALABI:v7p242/r6.anchor: فلما أرسل فرعون الذباحين لقتل موسى أخذوا الطريق الأعظم فجاء رجل من شيعة موسى من أقصى المدينة

THALABI:v7p242/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r7.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
THALABI:v7p242/r7.claim: Most exegetes identify the man as Hizqil ibn Sabura, a believer from Pharaoh's family and Pharaoh's cousin.
THALABI:v7p242/r7.anchor: فقال أكثر أهل التأويل: هو حزقيل بن صبورا مؤمن آل فرعون، وكان ابن عم فرعون،

THALABI:v7p242/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r8.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
THALABI:v7p242/r8.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi says the man was named Shamuʿun.

THALABI:v7p242/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r9.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p242/r9.claim: Another report gives the man's name as Shamʿan.
THALABI:v7p242/r9.anchor: فقال شعيب الجبائي: اسمه شمعون، وقيل:

THALABI:v7p242/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r10.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v7p242/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi says yasʿā means he hurried in his gait to warn Moses.
THALABI:v7p242/r10.anchor: قال الكلبي: يسرع في مشيه لينذره،

THALABI:v7p242/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r11.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p242/r11.claim: Muqatil says yasʿā means he walked on his feet.
THALABI:v7p242/r11.anchor: مقاتل: يمشي على رجليه، قال يا موسى إن الملأ

THALABI:v7p242/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p242/r12.claim: Yaʾtamirūna means they intend Moses's death and consult about him; another explanation is that they command one another, as in the verse about agreeing together kindly.
THALABI:v7p242/r12.anchor: أي يهمون بقتلك ويتشاورون فيك، وقيل: يأمر بعضهم بعضا نظيره قوله عز وجل: وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف،

THALABI:v7p242/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r13.speaker: النمر بن تغلب
THALABI:v7p242/r13.claim: Al-Nimr ibn Taghlib's verse is cited as evidence for the usage of yaʾtamirūna.
THALABI:v7p242/r13.anchor: نظيره قوله عز وجل: وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف، وقال النمر بن تغلب:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r2.claim: After hearing the Israelite’s accusation, the Egyptian went to the Copts and told them Moses was the killer; Pharaoh ordered Moses’ death, and a supporter warned him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r2.anchor: فلما سمع القبطي هذا من قول الإسرائيلي خلاه في يد موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man as Hizqil, a believing man from Pharaoh’s family; this is the majority exegetical view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: اسمه حزقيل، وهو الرجل المؤمن من آل فرعون. هذا قول أكثر المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the man was called Samʿan and does not identify him as a believer from Pharaoh’s family.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r4.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: يقال له: سمعان، ولم يذكر أنه المؤمن من آل فرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r5.claim: The phrase means from the farthest and most distant part of the city.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r5.anchor: {من أقصى المدينة} أي: من آخرها وأبعدها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r6.claim: Muqatil glosses the man’s coming as on foot.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the man’s coming as hurrying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يشتد. {قال يا موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r8.claim: The malaʾ are Pharaoh’s leading men and nobles.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r8.anchor: {قال يا موسى إن الملأ} يريد: الأشراف، يعني: أشراف قوم فرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda takes the verb to mean they are consulting about you in order to kill you, citing Rabiʿa ibn Jaʿsham’s verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r9.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: يتشاورون فيك ليقتلوك. واحتج بقول ربيعة بن جعشم النمري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects Abu Ubayda’s sense: the phrase means they intend evil against you, not that they consult; he cites poetry and 65:6 as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r10.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: وهذا غلط بين لمن تدبر، ومضادة للمعنى، كيف يعدو على المرء ما شاور فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r11.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the verb means that they are commanding one another to kill Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r11.anchor: وقال الزجاج في قوله: {يأتمرون بك} يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r12.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r12.claim: Al-Azhari says the verb means they command one another to kill him, a better lexical account than Ibn Qutayba’s “intend”; 65:6 likewise means command one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p363/r12.anchor: ومعنى: {يأتمرون بك} يؤامر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك؛ وهذا أحسن من قول القتيبي: إنه بمعنى: يهمون بك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r1.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r1.claim: Shammar says the verb can mean consulting someone or mutual consultation; consultation may be laudable with wise people, blameworthy when governed by desire, or fallible when one consults one’s own judgment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r1.anchor: ائتمرت فلانا في ذلك الأمر، إذا شاورته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r2.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r2.claim: Shammar cites the proverb about the confused person not knowing how to form an opinion, illustrating consultation with oneself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r2.anchor: ومنه المثل: (لا يدري المكذوب كيف يأتمر). أي: كيف يرى رأيا ويشاور نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi endorses Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj as essentially agreeing that the nobles are deliberating or directing one another to kill Moses; Ibn Qutayba’s gloss has no basis in the language.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r3.anchor: وقول أبي عبيدة والزجاج في تفسير: {يأتمرون} هو الصحيح، وقولهما قريب من السواء، وقول ابن قتيبة لا أصل له في اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi says Arabic does not use ائتمر بالشيء to mean merely intend it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p365/r4.anchor: ولا يقال: ائتمر بالشيء إذا هم به، ولم أر للمفسرين لفظا في تفسير الائتمار.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r1.claim: They specify that the intended victim is the Egyptian whom Moses killed the previous day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r1.anchor: قوله: {ليقتلوك} أي: بالقبطي الذي قتلته بالأمس. قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r2.claim: The warning means to leave the town; the man says he is sincere in advising Moses to go.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366/r2.anchor: {فاخرج} من القرية {إني لك من الناصحين} أي: في أمري إياك بالخروج

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r1.claim: The man who came running from the far end of the city was the believer from Pharaoh’s household.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r1.anchor: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى } وهو مؤمن آل فرعون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r2.claim: They were consulting together and telling one another to kill Moses.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r3.claim: The man advises Moses to leave that city, saying he is giving sincere advice.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r3.anchor: فاخرج } من هذه المدينة { إني لك من الناصحين }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains the man’s running as hurrying.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r3.anchor: {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} [القصص: 20] يعني يسرع، تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says the last Egyptian heard the Israelite mention yesterday’s killing and disclosed it; Pharaoh’s council then plotted Moses’ death.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: فأفشى عليه القبطي الذي هو عدو لهما أفشى عليه، فأتمر الملأ من قوم فرعون أن يقتلوه،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r5.claim: The man who warned Moses was the believer from Pharaoh’s household.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r5.anchor: فبلغ ذلك مؤمن آل فرعون، وهو الذي قال الله: {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين} [القصص: 20]

QASHANI:28:20-22/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:20-22/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:20-22/r1.claim: The man from the city's far edge is love that impels the journey to God, called will; he arises from the hidden store of preparedness when the self's desire is killed.
QASHANI:28:20-22/r1.anchor: هو الحب الباعث على السلوك في الله الذي يسمونه الإرادة

QASHANI:28:20-22/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:20-22/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:20-22/r2.claim: Love moves with unmatched speed, warning Moses of the faculties' domination and their plotting when imaginative power rises against him through disputation and misguidance.
QASHANI:28:20-22/r2.anchor: إذ لا حركة أسرع من حركته يحذره عن استيلائهم عليه وينبهه على تشاورهم وتظاهرهم عند ظهور سلطان الوهم عليه ومقابلته ومماراته ومجادلته له

QASHANI:28:20-22/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:20-22/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:20-22/r3.claim: Moses must leave the psychic city's bounds and rule for the station of spirit.
QASHANI:28:20-22/r3.anchor: عن مدينتهم حدود سلطنتهم إلى مقام الروح

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.claim: Once the Egyptian’s killer became known, Pharaoh ordered measures to capture Moses; a well-wisher ran to warn him and advise escape, so Moses left the city for Midian.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın iyiliğini düşünen bir kişi koşarak gelip bu durumdan onu haberdar etti ve şehirden çıkıp gitmesi için nasihatte bulundu

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r3.claim: An Israelite acquaintance hurried to Moses, saying the leaders were plotting to kill him, that he knew their plan, and that Moses should leave before they informed Pharaoh.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r3.anchor: جاء إسرائيلي من معارف موسى يسعى ، وقال إن القوم يريدون قتلك ، وأنا واقف على تدبيرهم

BURHAN:v4p90/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p90/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p90/r4.claim: Indefinite wording can denote one individual; رجل in the narrative introduces a single man.
BURHAN:v4p90/r4.anchor: واما التنكير فله اسباب الاول ارادة الوحدة نحو

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

ITQAN:v4p391/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r3.claim: The man who came running from the far end of the city is the believer from Pharaoh's people, named Shamaʿan, Shamaʿun, Jabr, Habib, or Hizqil.
ITQAN:v4p391/r3.anchor: هو مؤمن آل فرعون وإسمه شمعان وقيل شمعون وقيل جبر

ITQAN:v2p556/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r1.claim: The indefinite رجل in 28:20 signals one man: a single person came from the far end of the city.
ITQAN:v2p556/r1.anchor: أحدها إرادة الوحدة نحو ﴿ وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى ﴾

ITQAN:v2p556/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r2.claim: Indefiniteness can indicate a kind or type, as with a kind of reminder, an unusual covering, or a particular kind of life sought through future increase.
ITQAN:v2p556/r2.anchor: الثاني إرادة النوع نحو ﴿ هذا ذكر ﴾ أي نوع من الذكر

ITQAN:v2p556/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r4.claim: An indefinite may magnify something beyond specification, as in a war, painful punishment, greetings of peace, or gardens.
ITQAN:v2p556/r4.anchor: الثالث التعظيم بمعنى أنه أعظم من أن يعين ويعرف نحو ﴿ فأذنوا بحرب ﴾

ITQAN:v2p556/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r5.claim: Indefiniteness may signal abundance, as in a hoped-for great reward; it can combine abundance and greatness, as with many great messengers.
ITQAN:v2p556/r5.anchor: الرابع التكثير نحو ﴿ أئن لنا لأجرا ﴾ أي وافرا جزيلا

ITQAN:v2p556/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r7.claim: Indefiniteness can indicate small quantity: even a little divine approval exceeds the gardens, because it is the source of happiness; an unnamed poet says a little from you suffices.
ITQAN:v2p556/r7.anchor: السادس التقليل نحو ﴿ ورضوان من الله أكبر ﴾ أي رضوان قليل منه أكبر

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r18.claim: The man who came from the far side of the city is Ḥizqīl.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r18.anchor: " وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى " وهو حزقيل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.claim: The believer from Pharaoh’s family, including the man who warns Moses in the city, is identified as Ḥizqīl; another name given is Sharwān.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba gives أنى two near senses, 'how' and 'from where,' and says either may sometimes be construed as the other.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : أنى تكون لمعنيين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r2.speaker: الكميت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r2.claim: Al-Kumayt's verse is said to combine the senses 'how' and 'from where' in the same word.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r2.anchor: قال الكميت : - أنى ومن أين آبك الطرب … من حيث لا صبوة ولا ريب فجاء بالمعنيين جميعا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r3.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r3.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah says the interrogative is interpreted by context: time gives 'when,' a state gives 'how,' and a place gives 'where.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r3.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : أنى لفظ سؤال يرد في كل مكان بحسب ما يقتضيه من زمان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r5.claim: Yasʿā means he hurried in his walking.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r6.claim: Al-malaʾ refers to the leading men and notables.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r6.anchor: {قال يا موسى إن الملأ} يعني: الوجوه من الناس والأشراف (4) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads yaʾtamirūna as consulting together about killing Moses; Ibn Qutayba rejects this as contradicting the context, since consultation is good, and says it means they planned evil.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r7.anchor:
قال أبو عبيدة: (5) "يتشاورون فيك ليقتلوك". واحتج بقول الشاعر:
أحار بن عمرو! كأني خمر ... ويعدو على المرء ما يأتمر (6)
وهذا غلط بين لمن تدبر، ومضادة للمعنى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r1.claim: Yaʾtamirūna means they intend or plan to harm Moses, as shown by Ibn Tulub's poem about a muʾtamir who follows his own judgment and sometimes errs.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r1.anchor:
وقوله: {إن الملأ يأتمرون} أي يهمون بك. يدلك على ذلك قول النمر بن تولب:
اعلمن أن كل مؤتمر ... مخطئ في الرأي أحيانا (1)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r2.claim: In 65:6, waʾtamirū is interpreted as resolve on a good course, including that neither spouse harm the other, rather than consult one another.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r2.anchor: ومما يدلك على ذلك أيضا قوله عز وجل: {وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف} (2) لم يرد تشاوروا، وإنما أراد: هموا به، واعتزموا عليه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r3.claim: If Abū ʿUbayda's sense of mutual consultation were intended, the wording should instead be yataʾāmarūna fīka, consulting one another about you.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331/r3.anchor: ولو أراد المعنى الذي ذهب إليه أبو عبيدة، لكان أولى به أن يقول: "إن الملأ يتآمرون فيك" أي يستأمر بعضهم بعضا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r1.claim: In the account of the man coming from the city's outskirts, saʿy means hurrying on foot and can also mean running.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r1.anchor: أي يسرع في مشيه، وهو العدو أيضا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.claim: The common underlying sense of saʿy is walking and moving quickly.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.anchor: وأصل هذا كله: المشي والإسراع فيه

MAJAZ:v2p100/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p100/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p100/r1.claim: Yaʾtamirūna bika means they intend harm, confer, consult, and deliberate about you. Al-Namir b. Tawlab and Rabiʿah b. Jashm’s verses illustrate the verb; the latter notes that one’s apparent good judgment may bring ruin.
MAJAZ:v2p100/r1.anchor: «إن الملأ يأتمرون بك» (20) مجازه يهمون بك ويتوامرون فيك ويتشاورون فيك ويرتئون

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r1.claim: Yasʿā may be an adjective or circumstantial clause because the indefinite man has been specified by “from the outskirts”; if min aqṣā attaches to jāʾa, it can only be an adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون صفة، وأن يكون حالا؛ لأن النكرة قد تخصصت

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows only the adjective parse if min aqṣā is attached to jāʾa, following the majority grammatical position.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r2.anchor: قاله الزمخشري، بناء منه على مذهب الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r3.claim: The author notes Sībawayh allows the circumstantial parse without that restriction.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r3.anchor: أن سيبويه يجيز ذلك من غير شرط

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r4.claim: The phrase order differs from the man in 36:20: there he merely came from the far side, while here he is described as being from the outskirts; the two are different men and stories.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r4.anchor: وفي آية يس تقدم " من أقصى " على " رجل " لأنه لم يكن من أقصاها

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r5.claim: Yaʾtamirūn means they consult one another, as in al-Namir ibn Tawlab’s line using yuʾtamar.

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the meaning as people ordering one another, from the verse waʾtamirū baynakum bi-maʿrūf.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r6.anchor: وعن ابن قتيبة: يأمر بعضهم بعضا.

SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r7.claim: Lak may attach to an implied “advisor for you,” to al-nāṣiḥīn through broad adverb usage, or serve as an explicative phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:28:20/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بما يدل " الناصحين " عليه أي: ناصح لك من الناصحين

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r1.claim: A report identifies the man as a believer from Pharaoh's household and a carpenter.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r1.anchor: مؤمن آل فرعون، وإنه كان نجارا

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r3.claim: The ملأ are nobles and prominent people whom others look to.

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r4.claim: يأتمرون بك means they urge one another to kill Moses.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى يأتمرون بك يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r5.claim: لك is not governed by الناصحين, since a complement cannot precede its noun; it clarifies advice given for Moses' benefit.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r5.anchor: لأن الصلة لا تقدم على الموصول

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r6.claim: The construction means advising for someone's benefit; نصحت لك is more common than نصحتك.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r2.claim: In 36:20, placing “from the city's far end” before “a man” firmly says he came from there; in 28:20, the later phrase may describe either his origin or where he came from.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r2.anchor: (وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى) يعني هو فعلاً جاء من أقصى المدينة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r1.claim: ‘A man came from the far end of the city’ makes his place of origin definite; ‘a man from the far end came’ can mean either that he came from there or lived there.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r1.anchor: جاء من القرية رجل بمعنى أن مجيئه كان قطعيا من القرية وهذا تعبير قطعي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r2.claim: The less definite order in al-Qasas suits a man coming privately to warn Moses, unlike the man in Yasin who brings the public call to the whole city.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p756/r2.anchor: فالرجل جاء من أقصى المدينة للإسرار لموسى - عليه السلام -

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r1.claim: The Yasin visitor publicly calls a hostile town to follow the messengers, while the Qasas visitor privately warns Moses; no town-wide opposition to Moses is described.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r1.anchor: في القصص جاء ليسر في أذن موسى عليه السلام كلاماً (إن الملأ يأتمرون بك)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r2.claim: Because public proclamation is the more important mission, Yasin front-loads the man's arrival from the city edge; the warning to Moses is framed differently.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r2.anchor: فلما كان الموضوع أهمّ قدّم (جاء من أقصى المدينة) يحمل هم الدعوة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r3.claim: Since رجل is indefinite in both verses, يسعى is an adjective modifying the man in both; in al-Qasas من أقصى المدينة may be a first adjective and يسعى a second.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1102/r3.anchor: جملة (يسعى) صفة في آية يس وفي القصص (يسعى) صفة للرجل وليست للمدينة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#4/r1.speaker: author
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#4/r1.claim: The man who came running from the far end of the city is identified as a believer from Pharaoh’s household.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#4/r1.anchor: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى ﴾ قال هو مؤمن آل فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.claim: After this accusation spread to Pharaoh and his chiefs, they resolved to kill Moses; a believer from Pharaoh's family, his cousin, came to warn and advise him, leading into the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58/r2.anchor: ولما قال هذا انتشر الحديث وارتقى إلى فرعون وملائه فهموا بقتل موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.claim: The man from the city's outskirts is variously named Shimʿān, Shimʿūn son of Isḥāq, Ḥizqīl, or another name.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.anchor: واسمه قيل : شمعان وقيل : شمعون بن إسحاق وقيل : حزقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.claim: The well-known identification is that he was the believer from Pharaoh's family; another view identifies him as someone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.anchor: وكون هذا الرجل الجائي مؤمن آل فرعون هو المشهور وقيل هو غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.claim: The apparent meaning of yasʿā is that he hurried because he lived far away and was keen to warn and advise Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.anchor: ويسعى بمعنى يسرع في المشي وإنما أسرع لبعد محله ومزيد اهتمامه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.claim: Another reading takes yasʿā figuratively as seeking God's good pleasure, as in the wording of 17:19.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : يسعى بمعنى يقصد وجه الله تعالى كما في قوله سبحانه : ( وسعى لها سعيها )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.claim: Min aqṣā al-madīna most naturally modifies jāʾa; alternatively it describes the man, with yasʿā another adjective, or—with the phrase adjectival—yasʿā can be a circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن ( من أقصى ) صلة ( جاء ) وجملة ( يسعى ) صفة ( رجل )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.claim: If min aqṣā modifies jāʾa, most grammarians bar yasʿā as a circumstantial clause from the indefinite man; Sībawayh allows it because the prepositional phrase makes the noun definite-like.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.anchor: وأما إذا كان متعلقا بجاء فمنع ذلك الجمهور وأجازه سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.claim: Attaching min aqṣā to yasʿā is also proposed, but al-Ālūsī dismisses it as implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.anchor: وجوز أن يعلق الجار والمجرور بيسعى وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.claim: Al-malaʾ refers to the leading figures of Pharaoh's government.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.claim: Yaʾtamirūna bika means they are consulting about you; the term reflects each adviser both ordering and complying with the others, and their plan is to kill Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.anchor: أي يتشاورون بسببك وإنما سمي التشاور ائتمار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r10.claim: The lām in laka is clarifying and attaches to an omitted expression, like suqyā laka; most grammarians reject attachment to al-nāṣiḥīn because its al- is relative and the complement cannot precede it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r10.anchor: اللام للبيان كما في سقيا لك فيتعلق بمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r11.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r11.claim: Some grammarians allow laka to attach to al-nāṣiḥīn or to an implied term it explains, under analyses that permit advancing a complement before this al or treat it as a definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r11.anchor: وعند من جوز تقدم معمول الصلة إذا كان الموصول أل خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r12.speaker: القرطبي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r12.claim: Al-Qurṭubī and others infer from the verse that informing on someone is permissible when it serves a religious interest.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p58#2/r12.anchor: واستدل القرطبي وغيره بالآية على جواز النميمة لمصلحة دينية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r6.claim: The man who came was one of Moses’ adherents and came from the far end of the city.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r6.anchor: من شيعة موسى، {من أقصى المدينة} أي: من آخرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r7.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r7.claim: Most exegetes identify him as Ḥizbīl, a believer from Pharaoh’s household.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r8.claim: Other accounts name the man Shimʿūn or Shimʿān.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r9.claim: He was hurrying on foot, took a nearby route, reached Moses first, and warned him to use another route.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r9.anchor: أي: يسرع في مشيه، فأخذ طريقا قريبا حتى سبق إلى موسى فأخبره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r10.claim: The notables were consulting about Moses and planning his death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r10.anchor: يعني: أشراف قوم فرعون يتشاورون فيك، {ليقتلوك}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the expression as people ordering one another to kill Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r11.anchor: قال الزجاج: يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r12.claim: The man’s counsel was that Moses leave the city.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p198#2/r12.anchor: {فاخرج} من المدينة، {إني لك من الناصحين} في الأمر لك بالخروج

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r7.claim: After the accusation spread to Pharaoh and his council, who planned to kill Moses, a believer from Pharaoh's family, his cousin, came to warn him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r7.anchor: وهموا بقتله فخرج مؤمن آل فرعون وهو ابن عمه ليخبره

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r8.claim: يسعى means hastening; it is an adjective of رجل, or a circumstantial phrase if من أقصى المدينة is its adjective, not a complement of جاء because that qualification makes the noun definite-like.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r8.anchor: يسرع صفة رجل، أو حال منه إذا جعل من أقصى المدينة صفة له

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r9.claim: They are consulting about Moses; consultation is called يأتمر because each participant commands the others and follows their command.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r9.anchor: يتشاورون بسببك، وإنما سمي التشاور ائتمارا لأن كلا من المتشاورين

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r10.claim: The lām in لك clarifies the addressee; it is not governed by الناصحين, since a relative-clause complement cannot precede its relative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:19-20/r10.anchor: ل { النصحين } لأن معمول الصلة لا يتقدم الموصول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r1.claim: The wording places the subject before the phrase describing his arrival because the moment is grave; the order differs in Yasin.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r1.anchor: قدم فاعل المجيء على متعلقه بخلاف ما في سورة يس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r2.claim: The man who comes is one who loves Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r2.anchor: ممن يجب موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r3.claim: He comes from the city’s farthest edge, taking a shortcut and running so quickly that he outruns the others.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r3.anchor: أنه كان ماشيا بقوله : { يسهى } ولكنه اختصر طريقا واسرع في مشيته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r4.claim: The episode demonstrates divine power to take someone into dire danger and then bring sudden relief.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r4.anchor: من الأخذ بالخناق حتى يقول القائل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r5.claim: Calling Moses by name conveys affection and removes any uncertainty about whom he is addressing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r5.anchor: مناديا له باسمه تعطفا وإزالة للبس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r6.claim: The malāʾ are the Coptic nobles who hold authority to decide and command.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r6.anchor: أشراف القبط في أيديهم الحل والعقد , لأن لهم القدرة على الأمر والنهي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r7.claim: They are consulting about Moses until each commands the others and takes up their decision.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r7.anchor: حتى وصل حالهم في تشاورهم إلى أن كلا منهم يأمر الآخر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r8.claim: Their purpose is to kill Moses because they have heard that he killed one of their people.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r9.claim: The warning means Moses must leave this city.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r9.anchor: أي من هذه المدينة ؛ ثم علل ذلك بقوله على سبيل التأكيد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r10.claim: The man stresses that he is Moses’ sincere adviser to dispel any thought that danger is unlikely because Moses is favored by the king.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r10.anchor: على سبيل التأكيد ليزيل ما يطرق من احتمال عدم القتل لكونه عزيزا عند الملك

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the warning man as the believing member of Pharaoh's household.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} قال: مؤمن آل فرعون

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r6.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r6.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi says the man who warned Moses was named Shamaʿun.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r6.anchor: عن شعيب الجبائي قال: كان اسم الذي قال لموسى {إن الملأ يأتمرون بك} شمعون

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the man was not a notable and was called Hizqil.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} قال: يعمل ليس بالسيد اسمه حزقيل

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.claim: Al-Suddi recounts that a Copt exposed Moses to Pharaoh; while searchers pursued him through the byways, the warning man came, then an angel on horseback led Moses toward Midian after he prostrated in fear.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.anchor: عن السدي قال: ذهب القبطي فافشى عليه: أن موسى هو الذي قتل الرجل فطلبه فرعون وقال: خذوه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the arriving man as a believer from Pharaoh’s family.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك وجاء رجل من اقصى المدينة يسعى قال : مؤمن من ال فرعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies him as a partisan of Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : وجاء رجل من شيعة موسى من اقصى المدينة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r3.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r3.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī says the man who warned Moses was named Shamʿūn.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r3.anchor: عن شعيب الجبائي قال : كان اسم الذي قال لموسى : ان الملا ياتمرون بك شمعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Pharaoh and his chiefs had resolved to kill Moses; he names the arriving man Simʿān.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : واصبح الملا من قوم فرعون ، وفرعون قد اجمعوا لقتل موسى فيما بلغهم عنه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh sent executioners to kill Moses, while a partisan of Moses took a shortcut and reached him first with the warning.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فارسل فرعون الذباحين ليقتلوا موسى ، وهم لا يخافون ان يفوتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh ordered Moses seized for killing their man and told searchers to look in the side paths because Moses was young and would not know the roads.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2959#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي قال : فطلبه فرعون ، وقال : خذوه فانه قتل صاحبنا ، وقال للذين يطلبونه : اطلبوه في بنيات الطريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r1.claim: The man arrives during Moses’ exchange with the Egyptian, whose dialogue is omitted because a more important event interrupts the story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r1.anchor: جاء على حين محاورة القبطي مع موسى فلذلك انطوى أمر محاورتهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r2.claim: The city’s far end was likely Pharaoh’s palace quarter; rulers lived at city edges for safety from revolt or raids and easier escape, explaining the messenger’s location.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r2.anchor: أن أقصى المدينة هو ناحية قصور فرعون وقومه فإن عادة الملوك السكنى في أطراف المدن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r3.claim: Abu Tammam’s line about a city center becoming an edge means decline of settlement, a different sense from the city outskirts here.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r4.claim: Mentioning where the man came from also signals that he knew Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r4.anchor: وجه ذكر المكان الذي جاء منه الرجل وأن الرجل كان يعرف موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r5.claim: Al-malaʾ means influential people of consequence; here it denotes Pharaoh’s ruling elite, consulting about killing Moses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r6.claim: Their consultation implies the case reached Pharaoh; Exodus likewise says Pharaoh heard of it and sought Moses’ death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r6.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن القضية رفعت إلى فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r7.claim: The man hurried to warn Moses because he admired Moses’ uprightness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r7.anchor: أسرع بالخبر لموسى لأنه كان معجبا بموسى واستقامته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r8.claim: One reported possibility is that the man belonged to the Children of Israel.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r9.claim: Another possibility is that he was an Egyptian secretly believing; God may have guided his sound nature to recognize idolatry’s corruption and prepared him to save Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r9.anchor: كان من القبط ولكنه كان مؤمنا يكتم إيمانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r10.claim: Saʿy is rapid walking; the clause is circumstantial, describing the man who came from the city’s far end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r10.anchor: وجملة { يسعى } في موضع الحال من { رجل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p95/r11.claim: Yaʾtamirūna means consult, with an implied sense of intending; bi marks what they intend to do to Moses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r1.claim: Iʾtimār originally means accepting an order and came to mean consultation because each consultor accepts another’s proposal; Imruʾ al-Qays’s line describes harm from obeying one’s own command.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r2.claim: The consultation sense also appears in the command to consult together in what is right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r2.anchor: ثم شاع إطلاق الائتمار على التشاور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r3.claim: The sentence He said, Moses is a بدل اشتمال of the man’s arrival, since his arrival includes his speaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r3.anchor: لأن مجيئه يشتمل على قوله ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r4.claim: The destination of the command to leave is omitted but context supplies it: leave the city.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r5.claim: The assurance of sincere advice explains the command to leave; naṣaḥa commonly takes li, as in the verse about those who advised God and His Messenger, though direct-object usage also occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r5.anchor: لأن أكثر ما يستعمل فعل النصح معدى باللام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r6.claim: The prepositional phrase is brought forward to preserve the verse ending’s cadence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.claim: The episode teaches that God chooses whom He wills, prepares means to fulfill His purpose, and rescues His chosen messenger; upright conduct and love of truth disclose that care to the perceptive observer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.anchor: وأن الناظر البصير في آثار ذلك التدبير يقتبس منها دلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.claim: The signs in Moses’ story invite the Meccans to consider Muhammad’s character and their dealings with him, as the verse asks whether they reason about his lifetime among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.anchor: وفي ذلك كله مثل للمشركين لو نظروا في حال محمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.claim: The warning hints that Muhammad too will leave Mecca and that God will save him from his oppressors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.anchor: إيماء إلى أن رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيخرج من مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r7.claim: The warning messenger was said to be the believer from Pharaoh’s family or someone else; he took side streets to warn Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r7.anchor: وأخذ رجل يقال إنه مؤمن آل فرعون ويقال إنه غيره في بنيات الطريق قصد إلى موضع موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others say yasʿā means hurrying on foot, short of running.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r8.anchor: ويسعى معناه يسرع في مشيه قاله الزجاج وغيره وهو دون الجري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says yasʿā means working, not hurrying.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: معناه يعمل وليس بالشد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r10.claim: The author prefers hurrying here; the working sense is Mālik’s approach to Friday prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r10.anchor: وهذه نزعة مالك رحمه الله في سعي الجمعة والأول عندي أظهر في هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r11.claim: Yaʾtamirūn is iftaʿala, often mutual like tafaʿala, as izdawaja means tazāwaja.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r11.anchor: ويأتمرون وزنه يفتعلون ويفتعلون يأتي كثيرا بمعنى يتفاعلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it means command each other, arguing it should otherwise be yataʾammarūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r12.anchor: وذهل ابن قتيبة إلى أنه بمعنى يأمر بعضهم بعضا وقال: لو كان ذلك لكان يتأمرون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r13.claim: The author rejects Ibn Qutayba: iftaʿala can mean mutual action, as in 65:6 and al-Namr’s poetry.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r14.claim: Al-Namr ibn Tawlab’s verse witnesses the mutual sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p281#2/r14.anchor: وقد قال النمر بن تولب: [المتقارب] أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a poem using taʾtamiru for deliberation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r2.speaker: ربيعة بن جشم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r2.claim: Rabīʿa ibn Jusham’s verse also uses yaʾtamiru in a mutual or deliberative sense.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the messenger’s name as Shamaʿūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r10.anchor: وروى ابن جريج أن اسم الرجل الساعي من أقصى المدينة شمعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r11.claim: Ibn Isḥāq gives the messenger’s name as Shamaʿān.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r12.claim: The author considers firm claims about these names remote.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man as the believer from Pharaoh's household; his name is disputed in Surat Ghafir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وهذا الرجل هو مؤمن آل فرعون وسيأتي الخلاف في اسمه في سورة المؤمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r2.claim: Aqsa al-madina means the city's farthest part.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r5.claim: Al-malaʾ are the prominent people and chiefs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r5.anchor: فأما الملأ فهم الوجوه من الناس والاشراف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda says they were consulting about killing Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r6.anchor: أحدها يتشاورون فيك ليقتلوك قاله أبو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says they intended to harm Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r7.anchor: والثاني يهمون بك قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they were ordering one another to kill Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p210#2/r8.anchor: والثالث يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r1.claim: The man took a different, shorter route than Pharaoh's messengers and reached Moses first, which is why the verse describes him as a man of action.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r1.anchor: وصفه بالرجولية لأنه خالف الطريق، فسلك طريقا أقرب من طريق الذين بعثوا وراءه، فسبق إلى موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r2.claim: The elite are conferring together about Moses and intend to kill him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r2.anchor: {إن الملأ يأتمرون بك} أي: يتشاورون فيك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r3.claim: The man urges Moses to leave the city and assures him that his warning is sincere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226/r3.anchor: {ليقتلوك فاخرج} أي: من البلد {إني لك من الناصحين}

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r1.claim: One reported interpretation of yaʾtamirūna bika is “they are watching for you.”
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r1.anchor: قوله: (يأتمرون بك) قيل: معناه: يرقبونك، والكاف محله خفض بالباء.

JISHUMI:v8p5479/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5479/r2.claim: The pronoun kāf in bika is genitive because it follows the preposition bāʾ.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r1.claim: The man is identified in a report as the believing member of Pharaoh's family and Pharaoh's cousin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r1.anchor: قيل : الرجل : مؤمن آل مؤمن آل فرعون ، وكان ابن عم فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r2.claim: يسعى may modify رجل as an adjective or describe him circumstantially, since “from the far end of the city” has already specified him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r2.anchor: و { يسعى } يجوز ارتفاعه وصفا لرجل ، واتتصابه حالا عنه ؛ لأنه قد تخصص بأن وصف بقوله : { من أقصى المدينة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r3.claim: If جاء is followed by a relative clause, يسعى can only be adjectival.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r3.anchor: وإذا جعل صلة لجاء ، لم يجز في { يسعى } إلا الوصف .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r4.claim: ائتمار means consultation; each of two people advises or suggests something to the other.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r4.anchor: والائتمار : التشاور . يقال : الرجلان يتآمران ويأتمران ، لأن كل واحد منهما يأمر صاحبه بشيء أو يشير عليه بأمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r5.claim: The chiefs are consulting about Moses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r5.anchor: والمعنى : يتشاورون بسببك { لك } بيان ، وليس بصلة الناصحين .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404/r6.claim: لك clarifies الناصحين; it is not a complement governed by that word.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the man as a believer from Pharaoh's family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك : هو مؤمن آل فرعون . وقال شعيب : اسمه شمعون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r2.speaker: شعيب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r2.claim: Shuʿayb says the man's name was Shamaʿun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r2.anchor: وقال شعيب : اسمه شمعون . وقال محمد بن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq gives the man's name as Shamaʿan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق : شمعان . وقال الضحاك والكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r4.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi call him Hizqil ibn Shamaʿun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك والكلبي : اسمه حزقيل بن شمعون .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says he was Pharaoh's paternal cousin, the son of his father's brother.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي : هوابن عم فرعون أخي أبيه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets yaʾtamirūna as consulting together about killing Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r6.anchor: أحدهما : يتشاورون في قتلك , قاله الكلبي , ومنه قول النمر بن تولب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r7.speaker: النمر بن تولب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r7.claim: Al-Namir ibn Tawlab's line uses yuʾtamar to witness the sense of mutual deliberation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r7.anchor: ومنه قول النمر بن تولب : أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة … وفي كل حادثة يؤتمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r8.claim: A second explanation is that the council orders one another to kill Moses; 65:6 uses the same reciprocal verb for mutual exhortation to good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r8.anchor: الثاني : يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك ومنه قوله ^ { وأتمروا بينكم بالمعروف } ^ [ الطلاق : 6 ] أي ليأمر بعضكم بعضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r9.speaker: امرؤ القيس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r9.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line is cited as poetic evidence for the word's sense in the phrase wa-yaʿdū ʿalā al-marʾ mā yaʾtamir.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244/r9.anchor: وكقول امرىء القيس : أحار بن عمرو كأني خمر ويعدو على المرء ما يأتمر

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r1.claim: The man was the believing Copt Hizqil ibn Sabuth; he came running on foot from the far end of the town.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r1.anchor: فجاء حزقيل بن صابوث القبطي، وهو المؤمن

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r2.claim: Egypt’s chiefs conspired to kill Moses for killing the Copt, so the man urged him to leave and assured him of his sincere advice.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r2.anchor: { يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك } بقتلك القبطي، { فاخرج } من القرية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r1.claim: The man was the believer from Pharaoh's family, and Pharaoh's cousin.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r1.anchor: هو مؤمن آل فرعون وكان ابن عم فرعون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r2.claim: Yasʿā can be an adjective for rajul or a circumstantial clause; rajul already has the modifier from the city's outskirts.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r2.anchor: صفة لرجل أو حال من رجل لأنه وصف بقوله من أقصى المدينة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r3.claim: The leaders either urge one another to kill Moses or deliberate and consult about him; iʾtimār is mutual counsel, with each person advising the other.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r3.anchor: أي يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك أو يتشاورون بسببك والائتمار التشارو

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r4.claim: The man urges Moses to leave the city.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r5.claim: The phrase laka clarifies the counsel rather than modifying nāṣiḥīn, since a relative complement cannot precede its antecedent; it is like saying 'welcome to you.'
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#2/r5.anchor: لك بيان وليس بصلة الناصحين لأن الصلة لا تتقدم على الموصول

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r1.speaker: أكثر أهل التفسير
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the man as Hezekiel ibn Sabura, the believer from Pharaoh's family and Pharaoh's cousin; al-Thaʿlabi records this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r1.anchor: قال أكثر أهل التفسير: هذا الرجل هو حزقيل بن صبورا مؤمن آل فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r2.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli identifies the man as Talut; al-Mahdawi reports Qatada's identification as Shamʿun, and another view gives the name Shamʿan.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r2.anchor: وقيل: طالوت ذكره السهيلي. وقال المهدوي عن قتادة: شمعون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r3.speaker: الدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r3.claim: Al-Daraqutni says the name Shamʿan, with šīn, is known only as the believer from Pharaoh's family.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r3.anchor: قال الدارقطني: لا يعرف شمعان بالشين المعجمة إلا مؤمن آل فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r4.claim: A report says Pharaoh ordered Moses' execution, and the man hurried to warn him that the council was consulting about killing him for the Egyptian killed the previous day.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r4.anchor: وروي أن فرعون أمر بقتل موسى فسبق ذلك الرجل بالخبر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r5.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r5.claim: Al-Azhari says يأتمرون can mean that the council consults together or that its members command one another; the same root appears in 65:6 and in al-Nimr ibn Tawlab's poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r5.anchor: قال الأزهري: ائتمر القوم وتآمروا أي أمر بعضهم بعضا
